response: ## Accessibility Issue: Button missing accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2) **Bug ID:** `A11Y-3a2f1e8c` (instance) / `A11Y-3a2f1e8c` (pattern) **URL:** https://apply.ruralgrants.example.gov/application/step-2 **XPath:** `//button[contains(@class, 'doc-remove')]` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/main/div[2]/ul[@class='uploaded-docs']/li[3]/button[@class='doc-remove']` **WCAG SC:** 4.1.2 — Name, Role, Value (Level A) **Rule:** axe-core — button-name **Baseline test:** 5.C-ControlState **Severity:** Critical **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page **Screen type:** desktop | **Colour mode:** light ### HTML Snippet ```html ``` ### Description The "Remove document" button contains only an SVG icon with no accessible name. Screen reader users hear "button" with no indication of its purpose, making it impossible to understand or operate the control. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Go to https://apply.ruralgrants.example.gov/application/step-2 2. Wait for the page to load and locate the third item in the "uploaded-docs" list 3. Open VoiceOver (macOS) or NVDA (Windows) 4. Press Tab to move focus to the "doc-remove" button 5. Observe that the screen reader announces "button" with no additional information ### Expected Behaviour Expected: Screen reader announces "Remove document, button" or equivalent meaningful label. ### Actual Behaviour Actual: Screen reader announces "button" only. No accessible name is provided. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Chrome 126.0.0.0 | | OS | macOS 14.5 | | Screen reader | VoiceOver / NVDA | | Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 | ### Impact - Blind users cannot identify the button's purpose - Low-vision users relying on screen readers cannot operate the control - Users with motor impairments using voice control software cannot activate the button by speaking its label ### Suggested Fix Add an `aria-label` to the button element: ```html ``` Alternative: Add visually hidden text: ```html ``` --- **Labels:** accessibility, 508-audit, critical
